Q: preventDefault() inside a submit() event does not prevent the submission A:

Oddly enough, calling document.getElementById('contact-form').submit() doesn't trigger the submit() event. Since you're using jQuery, you can fix this by changing your 'Enviar' link to:

<a class="button" href="#" onClick="$('#contact-form').submit()">Enviar</a>

Once you've done that, remove the return false; located right after your e.preventDefault() line. It's causing the function to exit, preventing any code after it from running.

Q: Optional logging with a writer monad in haskell A:

Well... it would imply there's a memory leak: the program ends up using more memory than it ought to need because there's data that's dead but not so obviously dead that it gets collected.

I guess if you want to check whether it's happening, you can make a Foo value that requires a lot of memory, do a garbage collection (with performGC), and then check how much memory is being used (for example by running with the +RTS -T and calling getRTSStats). Try it with each approach and see if there's a difference.

Q: C standard: If `fgets` returns non-`NULL` but "encountered" end-of-file, will `feof` return true? A:

C standard: Can successful fgets() still set the EOF*3 indicator and return non-NULL?

Yes.

This happens when fgets(buf, n, stream) reads at least 1 character and the encounters end-of-file before reading a total of n-1 non-'\n' characters. See also @dbush

... one should only call feof() (and ferror()) once the return value of an I/O function actually indicated failure.

The 'should' idea is about right.

When fgets() returns non-NULL:

  1. Some characters read and an input error did not occur.

  2. *1

When fgets() returns NULL:

  1. An input error just occurred*2 - not that it occurred prior, Often this occurs on the first read attempt, yet may occur after a successful read of several characters.

  2. If the stream's end-of-file indicator is set. This usually means this is no more characters to be read, yet some streams will have more data after earlier reporting end-of-file.

  3. If the stream's end-of-file indicator is not set yet the first attempt to read a character results in an-end-fil file.

  4. *1

Use feof() first before ferror()

*1
Invalid buffer or stream pointers, closed stream or pathological cases of n <= 0, are also potential cases.

*2
Note that if ferror() is set, that unto itself does not cause fgets() to return NULL. If the input error is persistent, than NULL will be returned due to another input error.

*3 There is no EOF indicator. There are stream's two end-of-file and error indicators. Several functions like fgetc() return an int EOF to indicate end-of-file or error. I'll assume OP meant "set the end-of-file indicator".
